The authors employ z-score normalization to scale velocity and spin rate features, enabling meaningful comparison across pitch types without artificial transformation. A multivariable linear regression model is then applied to estimate how changes in these normalized features affect whiff rate. This regression framework allows for quantifying marginal contributions of velocity and spin rate, producing coefficients that guide tactical pitch selection. The practical optimization section applies these findings to specific pitchers, using z-scores to determine whether increasing or decreasing velocity/spin rate improves whiff rate. Dualities emerge in that while velocity alone may not strongly correlate with whiff rate, its interaction with spin rate does. Failure modes include overfitting due to small samples, misinterpretation of correlation as causation, and ignoring pitcher-specific variability. The model assumes linearity and normality, which may not hold universally across all pitch types or contexts.
